exposure: advanced maternal age (35-39 years, 40-44 years, 45+ years)
outcome: Apgar scores below seven at 5 min
cohort: The study included 312,221 singleton births to women aged 35 years and older in Sweden between 2010 and 2022, identified from the Swedish Medical Birth Register.
finding: Infants born to women aged 40-44 years and 45+ years had increased odds risks for adverse neonatal outcomes, including stillbirth, small for gestational age, preterm birth, low Apgar scores, and hypoglycaemia, compared to infants born to women aged 35-39 years.
